units.text: Two people can save valid updates to the same order, and still lose a change. Here's why. The shop's application writes order one thousand and one to S three. Once that write succeeds, another worker can retrieve the new order immediately. Listing the bucket reflects the update too. That is strong consistency: the completed write is visible.

Now suppose two workers open the same order. One changes the shipping address; the other marks the order as shipped. If both upload replacements, the later one can erase the earlier update. That's where a conditional write helps. It says: replace this object only if it still matches the E tag I read. If the match fails, review the newer version and resolve the conflict. Consistency tells you what you can see. It doesn't coordinate who can change it.
